clue.text: Two alcoholic drinks before my game

parts.note: gin is a spirit, the first of the two drinks
rum is another spirit, the second of the two drinks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a couple of drinks before settling down to their favourite game.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummy variant played with cards, popular as a two-player pastime, is a kind of game.

clue.text: Briefly scan glossy in which knight appears

indicators.note: the knight piece is placed within the word for glossy, so these words signal containment

parts.note: glacé means having a glossy, glazed finish, as of fruit or leather
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone flicks through a shiny magazine featuring a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is a link: the knight appears inside the word for glossy.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance at a page is to look at it quickly, a brief scan.

clue.text: Famous cathedral in Rome Dante misrepresented …

indicators.note: letters that are misrepresented are presented wrongly, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous cathedral in Rome is described wrongly by the poet Dante.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges ROMEDANTE; the cathedral is in Paris, not Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gothic church on the Île de la Cité in Paris is one of the world's best-known cathedrals.

clue.text: … excavate in chateau near there

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Continuing from the cathedral clue, someone digs in a French castle nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up out of the ground, a synonym for excavate.

clue.text: Join quite contrary girl across river

indicators.note: the girl's name stretches across the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' names the girl

explanation.surface: A contrary girl joins someone across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' is an English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed two people is to unite or join them in matrimony.

clue.text: All Blacks initially sit around filled with anger

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: to laze is to sit around idly

explanation.surface: The New Zealand rugby team sit about, furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The All Blacks are New Zealand's rugby team.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze figuratively describes someone burning with intense emotion such as fury.

clue.text: Expert has nothing on clown

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A skilled performer has nothing on a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a fool or jester who behaves ridiculously, like a clown.

clue.text: Very pale female wearing a number

indicators.note: the female pronoun is worn by, so enclosed in, the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman goes white while wearing a particular dress size.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, the grey pallor of ashes.

clue.text: Nervously meet seed, highly regarded

indicators.note: acting nervously suggests jittery movement, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A top seed, respected by all, meets an opponent with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone esteemed is held in great respect, a synonym for highly regarded.

clue.text: Don't see such a lot shining

definitions.meaning: read as two words, to ... is to see fewer things

explanation.surface: Something gleams so brightly it's hard to make much out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into SPOT (see) and LESS for the whimsical first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotless surface is clean and bright, so it can be called shining.

clue.text: Father had potato cooked just like that

indicators.note: something cooked has been worked over and altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad whipped up a potato in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly, without hesitation, which is what 'just like that' expresses.

clue.text: Without doubt, leader of competition left in good time

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: early means ahead of schedule, in good time

explanation.surface: The front-runner of a contest unmistakably got away ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearly as a sentence adverb means obviously, beyond any doubt.

clue.text: To thump counter is out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are not in their proper sequence, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hitting a shop counter is unacceptable behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat heavily, and thump also means defeat soundly.

clue.text: State of uproar in duma, so he agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up or shaken, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Russian parliamentarian stirs things up, causing chaos in the Duma.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duma is the Russian parliament; 'agitated' rearranges DUMASOHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A madhouse figuratively describes a scene of chaos and noisy confusion.

clue.text: Weaker party, a French boxer perhaps holding the German

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the German article between them

parts.note: un is the French for a
a boxer is a breed of dog
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A French boxer is cast as the outsider in a fight with a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the boxer as one example of a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog is the competitor expected to lose, the weaker side in a contest.

clue.text: Sound of hooter I installed

indicators.note: the letter I is put in place inside the other word

parts.note: hooter is British slang for nose

explanation.surface: A car horn has been fitted and makes its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any audible sound, often an unwanted one.

clue.text: Fashionable French writer's introduction to small northern city

parts.note: in means fashionable, in vogue
Jules Verne was a French novelist; with the possessive S

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trendy French novelist's opening work is set in a small town in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland capital in northern Scotland is a city, granted that status in 2000.

clue.text: The cows, roaming round quiet Welsh town

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the letter for quiet
roaming cows wander about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Cattle wander quietly around a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming' turns THECOWS into CHESTOW, and 'round' puts it around P.
explanation.definitionFit: Chepstow is a town in Monmouthshire on the River Wye, known for its racecourse.

clue.text: Wedges demonstrated by male champion golfer

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
Ernie Els is a South African major-winning golfer

explanation.surface: A golfing champion shows off his skill with wedge clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Wedges are golf clubs in the surface but shoes here.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedges are shoes with a solid wedge-shaped sole, a type of raised footwear.

clue.text: Looking after number one son, doctor flies to reach hospital

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A son's medic flies in to reach the hospital and care for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after number one is an idiom for putting oneself first, being self-centred.

clue.text: Break down or break up?

definitions.meaning: to decompose or melt away into solution
to end or disband, as of a marriage or parliament

explanation.definitionFit: Dissolve covers both senses: a substance breaking down in liquid and an assembly being formally disbanded.

clue.text: Outdoor work — rain affected having dogged energy

indicators.note: to dog is to follow closely, so the shuffled rain comes after the energy letter

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
E is the symbol for energy in physics

indicators.note: affected means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Outdoor work is hampered by rain but continues with stubborn energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges RAIN into NAIR; 'dogged' looks like 'determined' but means 'followed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outside rather than under a roof, i.e. outdoor.

clue.text: Artwork of Nehru finally acquired by nation

indicators.note: the final letter is taken in by the nation word

parts.note: a state is a nation

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sculpture of Nehru, India's first prime minister, is bought by the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a classic piece of art.

clue.text: In university in part of London

indicators.note: the university letter is placed in the district's name

parts.note: Poplar is a district in East London

explanation.surface: Someone studies at a university in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable or in favour, and so does widely liked.

clue.text: Game fighter's end following jab

indicators.note: the last letter comes after the jab word

parts.note: a poke is a jab or prod

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A boxer's career ends after a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game involving betting and bluffing.

clue.text: Clown and I make a mistake filling container

indicators.note: the I and the mistake word fill the container word

parts.note: a pot is a container
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A clown and I blunder while filling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: Steps king's installed in a dock to get up

indicators.note: the king letter is installed inside the reversed letters
in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to lop is to cut off or dock
K is the chess abbreviation for king; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A king is put in a dock and made to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns A LOP into POLA, and K goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A polka is a lively dance, a set of steps from Bohemia.

clue.text: Options for gin drinker or thief? Please yourself

definitions.text: Options for gin drinker or thief?
definitions.meaning: a drinker may accept a glass or decline it; a thief may steal an item or not
an expression of indifference: do as you like

explanation.surface: A drinker and a thief each face a choice, told to suit themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase offers a choice with indifference, meaning do whatever you like.

clue.text: Throw out Yankee dignitary

indicators.note: out here signals letters thrown out of their order

parts.note: Yankee is the NATO alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: A dignitary from America is ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthy is a notable person of local importance, a dignitary.

clue.text: A pass splitting the French in game

indicators.note: the inserted letters split the French article apart

parts.note: le is French for the
taken as written
a cross is a pass across the field in football

explanation.surface: A pass divides the French team in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field sport played with netted sticks.
